A publishing house of record.

Founded in 1947, KLB is a State corporation that publishes, prints and distributes the books Kenya learns from, and has done so through every curriculum the country has known.

100% government owned

sections.label: Our story
sections.html:
Our story

From the East African Literature Bureau to Kenya's largest textbook publisher.

KLB is home to authors, researchers and publishing specialists. We provide educational publications ranging from school and college textbooks to dictionaries, autobiographies, storybooks and e-books, alongside high-end printing services.

We publish in different languages and offer translation services. Our head office is in South C, Nairobi, with a Sales and Customer Service branch on Kijabe Street and field staff across the country.

The Bureau was established in 1947 as the East African Literature Bureau. It became the Kenya Literature Bureau PLC in 1980 and is wholly owned by the Government of Kenya.

Publishing & printing for you.

Manuscript development, editorial, design, translation, offset and digital printing, distribution and digital editions: one institution, end to end.

An academic tour at KLB's Nairobi press: publishing and printing in one place.

sections.label: Mandate
sections.html:
Our mandate

What the Act requires of us.

The mandate of the Bureau is set out in the Kenya Literature Bureau Act, Cap 209 (Revised 2012).

Kenya Literature Bureau Act, Cap 209

Download the Act (PDF) · Governance documents

  1. Carry on the business of publishing, printing and distributing literary, educational, cultural and scientific books, periodicals, journals, magazines, digital and electronic materials, and works of every description.
  2. Acquire copyrights in and rights and licences over literary and other works of every description.
  3. Promote, through appropriate government agencies, the production of low-cost adult literacy, educational, cultural and scientific literature and materials and make them available for distribution within and outside Kenya.
  4. Promote, encourage and assist authors within and outside Kenya, through financial incentives or otherwise, to publish scholarly works.
  5. Make available for general readership, through translation from foreign to local languages, works of interest and value to the public.
  6. Organise competitions in respect of literary contributions suitable for publication by the Bureau and grant prizes or rewards on such terms as it may deem fit.
  7. Co-operate with other bodies engaged in publishing, printing and distribution of books, periodicals, journals and magazines.
  8. Publish, print and sell educational materials at reasonable prices so as to make them available to schools and other educational institutions.
  9. Do all such things as appear to be necessary, desirable or expedient for the proper discharge of its functions under the Act.

sections.label: Procurement process
sections.html:
How procurement works

From advertisement to award.

Requirements

Requirements are specified in each tender document. Firms are generally expected to demonstrate competence through experience, capacity and statutory compliance. Some opportunities are open to all firms; others are reserved for special groups, which must provide evidence of registration in the relevant group.

Bid documents

Once advertised, bidders pay the required fee, collect the document and attach the receipt to the tender on submission. Documents are also available for download; downloaded bids require payment and a receipt. Pre-qualifications are downloaded and submitted free of charge.

Evaluation and award

After closing, KLB evaluates bids and issues notifications. Award is made to the firm offering the lowest evaluated price, not necessarily the lowest price alone. Successful firms normally enter a framework contract, with goods ordered as required through a Local Purchase Order.

Quotations

For pre-qualifications, quotations are invited from shortlisted firms as needs arise. Not every qualified firm is assured of business; KLB aims to invite as many firms as practical whenever opportunities arise.

Special groups

KLB reserves some opportunities for firms registered under the Access to Government Procurement Opportunities (AGPO) programme and other special groups. Read the procurement guidelines for special group firms (PDF).

Integrity in procurement

KLB expects suppliers to act ethically and in compliance with the Anti-Bribery and Corruption Act. Report suspected corruption through the Bureau's official channels.

Closed notices

Older disposal and sale notices from 2024 have closed. Archived notices are available from Supply Chain Management on request.

sections.label: Page hero
sections.html:
Home/Privacy

Legal

Privacy policy

How Kenya Literature Bureau PLC collects and uses information on this website.

sections.label: Privacy notice
sections.html:
Who we are

This website is operated by Kenya Literature Bureau PLC (KLB). Our website address is https://klb.co.ke.

What information we collect

Enquiry forms: When you use the contact form, we collect the details you submit (name, email, phone, organisation, enquiry type and message) so we can respond to your request.

Newsletter: If you subscribe to the newsletter, we collect your email address.

Website logs: Like most websites, our hosting environment may log standard technical information (such as IP address, browser type and pages requested) for security and reliability.

Cookies: This redesign does not rely on third-party advertising cookies. If cookies are used for basic site functionality, they are used to keep the site working as expected.

How we use information

We use the information you provide to respond to enquiries, process requests you make, send newsletter updates if you subscribe, and to maintain the security and performance of the website.

Sharing

We do not sell your personal information. We only share information when necessary to respond to your request (for example, routing an enquiry to the right team) or when required by law.

Data retention

We keep enquiry emails and submissions for as long as reasonably necessary to handle your request and meet our record-keeping obligations.

Your rights

You may ask us to correct or delete information you have provided by contacting info@klb.co.ke.

Links to other sites

This website links to third-party sites (including klbbooks.com and digital partners). We are not responsible for the privacy practices of those sites.

Updates

This policy may be updated from time to time. The date of the latest update appears on this page.

Last updated: November 2026.

Terms of sale

Key terms that apply when purchasing books and products from Kenya Literature Bureau PLC. The full published terms remain the controlling document.

sections.label: Terms of sale
sections.html:
Current price list (PDF) · Contact customer service

Summary

  • Orders are subject to KLB's published terms and conditions of sale.
  • Prices may change without notice; VAT applies where chargeable.
  • Credit facilities are granted at KLB's discretion and subject to its credit policy.
  • Delivery terms depend on whether goods are sold carriage-paid or ex-warehouse.
  • Claims for shortages or damage must be made within the time limits set in the terms.
  • Goods remain subject to the conditions published by KLB until payment terms are met as agreed.

Full terms and conditions

The complete, published Terms and Conditions of Sale for Kenya Literature Bureau PLC are retained for reference. If there is any difference between this summary and the published document, the published terms apply.

Request the full document

If you need a copy of the current Terms and Conditions of Sale for a specific transaction, email customer@klb.co.ke or contact the Kijabe Street customer service centre.

Orders and enquiries

For orders, availability and account registration, use the contact form or call 020 2684941-4.

Last updated: November 2026.
